entries.name: Urgency Pressure
entries.definition: Using time pressure or demands for immediate action to reduce the opportunity for careful consideration or independent verification.
indicators: Demands to act immediately
Short deadlines paired with requests for sensitive information or actions
Repeated insistence that there is no time to verify a request
entries.example: Send me the verification code immediately. You have only five minutes.
entries.interpretation: Assess whether urgency is being used to push a consequential action, especially when paired with credential requests, threats, or discouragement of verification.
entries.distinction: A genuine time-sensitive situation may involve urgency without manipulation. Urgency alone is not proof of malicious intent.
recommended_actions: Pause before taking the requested action
Verify consequential requests through an independent trusted channel
Avoid sharing passwords, one-time codes, or other sensitive credentials

entries.name: Fear-Based Persuasion
entries.definition: Using threats, alarming consequences, or fear-inducing claims to influence a person's decision or prompt compliance.
indicators: Threats of account closure, financial loss, punishment, or other serious consequences
Repeated alarming claims intended to prompt a response
Warnings that discourage the person from delaying or verifying
entries.example: If you do not provide the code now, your account will be frozen and you may lose your funds.
entries.interpretation: Look for fear-inducing consequences linked to a requested action, and whether the claim can be independently verified.
entries.distinction: Legitimate warnings can describe real risks. The presence of a warning alone does not establish coercion or deception.
recommended_actions: Do not act solely because of a threatening message
Check the claim with the relevant organization using independently obtained contact details
Keep a record of suspicious communications

entries.name: Impersonation
entries.definition: Claiming or implying an identity, role, or affiliation that is not genuine in order to gain trust or influence another person's actions.
indicators: Claims to represent a bank, government agency, employer, platform, or trusted individual
Requests for sensitive information based on an asserted role
Identity claims that cannot be independently verified
entries.example: I am calling from your bank's security department. I need to verify your account.
entries.interpretation: Identify the claimed identity and any consequential requests made under that identity. The transcript alone may not establish whether the claim is false.
entries.distinction: A person legitimately representing an organization is not impersonating it. Verification is needed before treating an identity claim as deceptive.
recommended_actions: Verify the person's role through the organization's official channels
Do not disclose credentials or one-time codes to an unverified contact
Avoid using contact details supplied only in the suspicious message

entries.name: Emotional Manipulation
entries.definition: Using emotional appeals, such as guilt, affection, shame, or sympathy, to influence a person's decisions in a way that may undermine their ability to choose freely.
indicators: Guilt-inducing statements tied to compliance
Affection or approval made conditional on taking an action
Repeated emotional appeals used to override expressed hesitation
entries.example: If you really cared about me, you would send the money without asking questions.
entries.interpretation: Consider whether an emotional appeal is being used to pressure a specific decision, particularly after the person expresses doubt or sets a boundary.
entries.distinction: Expressing genuine emotions, asking for support, or discussing relationship concerns is not automatically manipulative.
recommended_actions: Take time to consider the request independently
Seek perspective from a trusted person when feeling pressured
Maintain personal boundaries and avoid rushed financial or sensitive decisions

entries.name: Financial Extraction
entries.definition: Attempting to obtain money, payment credentials, financial account information, or other financially valuable information through a conversation.
indicators: Requests for money, transfers, gift cards, or cryptocurrency
Requests for account numbers, payment details, or banking credentials
Requests to provide one-time codes or approve transactions
entries.example: Please send the payment to this account now so we can prevent your service from being suspended.
entries.interpretation: Identify what financial asset or information is being requested, who is requesting it, and what justification is provided.
entries.distinction: Legitimate payments and financial administration also involve requests for money or account details. Context and independent verification matter.
recommended_actions: Verify payment instructions through a trusted, independent channel
Do not share passwords, PINs, or one-time verification codes
Contact the financial institution promptly if sensitive information has already been disclosed

entries.name: Trust Engineering
entries.definition: Building or leveraging perceived trust, familiarity, authority, or shared interests to make a person more willing to accept a request.
indicators: Repeated attempts to establish credibility or special familiarity
Claims of shared connections, insider knowledge, or privileged access
Use of established rapport to support a consequential request
entries.example: You know you can trust me. We have worked together for years, so just approve this request.
entries.interpretation: Assess whether trust-building language is being used to support a request that would otherwise warrant scrutiny.
entries.distinction: Building genuine rapport and demonstrating credibility are normal parts of communication. Trust-building language alone does not prove manipulation.
recommended_actions: Evaluate the request separately from the relationship
Verify unusual or high-impact requests independently
Be cautious when familiarity is used as a substitute for verification

entries.name: Social Isolation
entries.definition: Discouraging or preventing a person from seeking outside advice, verification, or support in connection with a consequential request.
indicators: Instructions not to tell friends, family, colleagues, or relevant authorities
Claims that the person must handle the matter alone
Discouraging independent contact with an organization or trusted adviser
entries.example: Do not contact the bank or tell anyone about this investigation. You must follow my instructions only.
entries.interpretation: Look for attempts to restrict access to independent advice or verification, especially when sensitive information or money is involved.
entries.distinction: Requests for ordinary confidentiality can be legitimate. The concern increases when secrecy is used to prevent reasonable verification or support.
recommended_actions: Seek independent advice when a request feels suspicious
Contact the relevant organization using official contact details
Do not let a demand for secrecy prevent appropriate safety checks

entries.name: Coercion
entries.definition: Using threats, intimidation, forceful demands, or the threatened imposition of consequences to compel a person to act against their wishes.
indicators: Threats linked directly to compliance or refusal
Repeated forceful demands despite expressed hesitation
Statements that remove or undermine the person's ability to decline freely
entries.example: Send me the code now, or I will make sure you lose access to your account.
entries.interpretation: Look for a clear connection between a demand and a threatened consequence. Consider the surrounding turns and the person's response.
entries.distinction: A firm request, legitimate policy consequence, or ordinary disagreement is not automatically coercion. The context and nature of the pressure matter.
recommended_actions: Avoid complying with threats without independent verification
Disengage if the interaction feels unsafe
Seek help from the relevant organization or appropriate support service when needed
